label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — The sink at L69-L70 writes the concatenation of sql directly to the HTTP response writer. Although ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(sql) is called, the CodeQL flow indicates the sink captures the raw concatenated string ('... + ...') before the encoded result replaces it in the final output. Thus, the resolved sink value is attacker-controlled (contains unsanitized param). Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-TP — The sink at L51 (variable sql) receives user input via param -> valuesList -> bar -> sql. The guard condition (if param != null) allows param to enter valuesList, and valuesList.get(1) retrieves the second element (which is param since index 0 is removed). Therefore, the resolved sink value for sql is the user-supplied param, leading to SQL injection. Since both alerts are TP, the case label is TP.
